description: When Wed Sep 30 7pm — 9pm Central Where Classroom - North Lobby Details Beginner-Friendly Woodworking: Carve Your Own Chopsticks Host Liam Luu Cost $0.00 For over 5,000 years, chopsticks have been the utensil of choice for billions of people around the globe. Now, it’s your turn to connect with that ancient tradition in a completely new way—by crafting your very own pair from scratch. Step into the woodworking workshop where you will craft a completely custom set of chopsticks. There is an incredible thrill in transforming a raw block of wood into a sleek, finished tool. Eating your favorite sushi or noodle dish with a utensil you shaped with your own two hands doesn't just look incredibly cool—it makes every single meal taste a little bit better. What You’ll Experience: Select Your Canvas: You'll get to pick from a stunning lineup of rich, exotic hardwoods. Whether you are drawn to the classic warmth of maple, cherry, and walnut, or the striking, deep tones of bloodwood and purpleheart, you’ll find the perfect wood to match your personal style. Hand Plane: Experience the incredibly fun, tactile thrill of traditional woodworking. You will learn how to properly angle and use a hand plane to shave away delicate ribbons of wood, slowly tapering your raw blank into a perfectly balanced chopstick. Sand & Finish: We will guide you through the satisfying process of sanding your chopsticks to a buttery-smooth finish and sealing them to make the natural wood grain truly pop. Why You'll Love It: Whether you are making a set to upgrade your own kitchen or crafting a deeply personal, one-of-a-kind gift for someone special, you will leave this workshop with a functional piece of art. This class is beginner-friendly, incredibly fun, and seats are strictly limited. Come experience the joy of woodworking and leave with a masterpiece you can use every day!

title: simple fold forming copper
description: When Thu Oct 1 7pm — 10pm Central Where Workshop - Jewelry / Small Metals - Small Low-top Work Table Details simple fold forming technique to put a ridge in your metal Host sue rogers Cost $0.00 We will cut a copper shape and fold it, then hammer the fold. description: When Sat Oct 3 11am — 12:30pm Central Where Lab - Science - Chemistry Details Handmade & One-of-a-Kind: Cold Process Soap Workshop Host Liam Luu Cost $0.00 Unlock the art and science of soap making in this can’t-miss, hands-on cold process workshop! In this engaging and beginner-friendly class, you’ll learn how to create beautiful, long-lasting bar soap from scratch using the cold process method—the gold standard for artisan soap makers. We’ll guide you step-by-step through the entire process, from selecting oils to safely working with lye, so you feel confident every step of the way. But this isn’t just about following a recipe—we’ll dive into the fascinating science of saponification, giving you a clear understanding of how simple ingredients transform into a gentle, effective cleansing bar. Once you understand the “why,” you’ll be empowered to experiment and create your own custom recipes. Then comes the fun: personalization! You’ll blend your own fragrance, choose your style, and craft a truly one-of-a-kind soap that reflects your creativity. By the end of the workshop, you won’t just leave with your own handmade soap curing and ready to use—you’ll walk away with the confidence, knowledge, and skills to become self-sufficient, making and customizing soap at home for yourself, your family, or even as gifts. Syllabus: -What is saponification -What are surfactant -Type of fats and oils in soap-making -Quality of each fat and oil -Saturated vs. Unsaturated fats -Type of lye; NaOH vs KOH -Hot Process vs Cold Process Soap -Step by Step instruction on making Soap -Adding Fragrance -Understanding pH -Aging your soap

title: Epoxy Charcuterie Board Workshop - $180.00
description: When Fri Oct 9 7pm — 10pm Central Where Workshop - Open Table Area South Details In this hands-on class, you will design and create a custom wood-and-epoxy charcuterie board from start to finish, covering material selection, safe epoxy handling, pouring techniques, and food-safe finishing. This is a project-based class; everyone Host HB Smart II Cost $0.00 Location: Dallas Makerspace – South Work area Duration: 2 sessions, 2–3 hours each (Session 1: Deep pour epoxy) Session 2: flatten, shape, and finish) Same time the following: Class 2: Thursday - 10/16 @ 7:00 pm Finish is self-paced after the Armor seal is applied ***Please read to the bottom*** Prerequisites: Age 16+ (or per DMS youth policy with guardian) Skill Level: No prior epoxy experience required; basic tool comfort helpful but not required. Materials: Deep Pour Epoxy, pigments, wood blanks, and finish provided Board Size: Approx. 12" x 18" x 1 By the end of this class, students will be able to: Identify suitable wood species and moisture requirements for epoxy charcuterie boards. Safely measure, mix, color, and pour epoxy resin for a “river” DEEP POUR Epoxy. Use common woodworking tools (planer, table saw, router, and sanders) to flatten, trim, and shape an epoxy board. Sand through appropriate grits and apply a food-safe finish for serving use. Understand basic care and maintenance for epoxy serving boards Session 1 – Design, Prep, and Pour Focus: Design, material prep, and epoxy work. Safety and Orientation (15–20 minutes) Brief overview of shop rules and PPE for epoxy and woodworking tools. Discussion of ventilation, skin protection, and cleanup for epoxy resin. Board Design and Wood Prep (30–45 minutes) Choosing board layout: straight river, offset river, or inlay-style epoxy feature. Inspecting wood for defects, cracks, and moisture issues that affect epoxy bonding. Cutting and fitting pieces into a mold or form pre-cut blanks Mold Setup and Sealing (15–30 minutes) Overview of forms, tape, and sealants to prevent leaks. Clamping or weighting the workpiece to prevent float in the pour. Epoxy Mixing, Coloring, and Pour (45–60 minutes) Measuring resin and hardener by volume or weight and mixing to manufacturer specs. Adding pigments or mica powders; demo of swirl vs solid-color techniques. Pouring, leveling, and basic bubble management (torch/heat gun if allowed, or alternative methods). Wrap-Up (5–10 minutes) Curing time expectations and when to return for Session 2 (7 days minimum). Quick Q&A and review of next session’s steps (flatten, shape, finish) Session 2 – Flattening, Shaping, and Finishing -7/18/2026 Focus: Turning the cured blank into a finished, food-safe board. Demold and Initial Assessment (10–15 minutes) Releasing the board from the form and checking for voids, sharp edges, or defects. Flattening and Trimming (30–45 minutes) Hands on - flattening techniques: planer Planner uses Squaring edges, trimming to final dimensions on table saw or miter saw. Shaping and Edge Profiles (20–30 minutes) Routing a profile on edges (round-over, chamfer, etc.) and softening corners. Sanding and Surface Prep (30–40 minutes) Progressing through grits appropriate for wood/epoxy (e.g., 80–220+). Tips to avoid swirl marks and to blend epoxy and wood surfaces. Food-Safe Finish (15–20 minutes) Applying a food-safe oil/wax finish and buffing to a soft sheen. Quick discussion of re-oiling schedule and general care (no dishwasher, avoid prolonged soaking, etc.). Finishing is completed at self -paced daily at the space 10 minutes every 24 hrs until you can take your board home. 3 to 4 coats. Brief overview of how laser engraving can be added later for personalization. Because this class uses high-end materials, including MAS Deep Pour Epoxy, mica powders, and inks, the material costs are significant. Through hands-on practice and instructor guidance, you’ll learn to recognize what is happening on the wheel and develop the tools to troubleshoot and improve. description: When Sun Oct 11 11am — 1pm Central Where Workshop - Ceramics & Jewelry Flex Details From Ming to Delft: The Art of Blue & White Tile Painting Host Liam Luu Cost $0.00 In the 17th century, Europe was swept by a craze for imported Chinese blue and white porcelain. Its pristine white surfaces and intricate, brilliant blue designs were the ultimate symbol of wealth and refined taste. But when international trade routes were interrupted, clever potters in the Dutch city of Delft saw an incredible opportunity. To satisfy the massive demand, they developed a brilliant local alternative: they coated earthenware in an opaque white tin-glaze and painted it with striking cobalt oxide. This ingenious response didn't just mimic the Chinese originals—it birthed the iconic, world-renowned tradition of Dutch Delftware. Discover the magic of cobalt in this hands-on tile painting workshop! Whether you are a seasoned potter or a complete beginner looking for a creative outlet, you'll learn the centuries-old techniques used to create these iconic blue and white masterpieces. In this immersive, beginner-friendly class, you will: Master the Cobalt Wash: Learn how this powerful mineral—which looks pale and unassuming when applied—transforms in the heat of the kiln into that unmistakable, vivid "Delft Blue." Practice Traditional Brushwork: We'll cover the specific strokes, shading, and line work used by 17th-century artisans. Design Your Masterpiece: Choose from classic Dutch motifs (like tulips, windmills, and sailing ships) or sketch your own modern design. Paint Your Own Tile: You will hand-paint a pre-glazed tile using pure cobalt pigment, ready to be fired in our kilns. You will leave this class with a beautiful, custom-painted Delft-style tile of your very own—perfect for a coaster, a decorative wall piece, or the beginning of your own tile backsplash. No prior painting or pottery experience is required. All materials, including tiles, brushes, and cobalt glazes, are provided!

title: Woodshop: Build a Farmhouse End Table with a Hidden Compartment (8-Week Series)
description: When Mon Oct 12 7pm — 10:30pm Central Where Workshop - Open Table Area South Details Build a Farmhouse End Table with a Hidden Compartment - $550.00 Host HB Smart II Cost $0.00 Over eight weeks you'll build your own solid wood farmhouse end table with a hidden storage compartment built into the top. From the outside it looks like a regular end table. Underneath the top is a secret space for valuables, remotes, or anything else you'd rather keep out of sight. Class schedule: Oct 12th - 7 pm OCT 19th - 7 pm Oct 26th - 7 pm Nov 2nd - 7 pm Nov. 9th - 7 pm Nov. 16th -7 pm Nov. 23rd -7 pm Nov. 30th - 7 pm Please pay in advance to reserve your spot: $550.00 https://www.venmo.com/u/HB-Smart You do the work yourself, and you get hands-on, one-on-one coaching inside a small group. We start with rough lumber and follow the full process. You'll mill boards flat and square, glue up a solid top, cut strong joinery, build the hidden compartment and its opening mechanism, and put on a durable finish. Along the way you'll get comfortable with the jointer, planer, table saw, miter saw, and router table. The goal is to get you past any fear of the equipment and leave you with a healthy respect for it. Many students go on from here to build bigger pieces like coffee tables, dining tables, and beds. Week-by-week plan: Design and lumber selection: Go over the plans and the compartment layout, make a cut list, pick boards, and rough-cut them to size. Milling: Use the jointer and planer to make stock flat, straight, and square. Tabletop glue-up: Arrange the boards for the best grain, glue up, and clamp the top. Legs: Cut the legs to size and shape or taper them for the farmhouse look. Joinery: Cut the apron joints that connect the legs and aprons. Concealment compartment: Build the hidden box under the top and fit the opening mechanism so the gaps stay tight and nothing gives it away. Assembly and dry fit: Glue up the base, add the lower shelf, and test how the compartment opens and closes. Finishing: Sand, apply stain or finish, do the final fitting of the top, and take your table home.

title: Ceramic Arts: How to Glaze your Bisque Pottery
description: When Wed Oct 14 7:30pm — 9pm Central Where Workshop - Ceramics Main Area Details learn how to glaze your bisqueware Host Liam Luu Cost $0.00 Step into the final, transformative stage of pottery—glazing. This hands-on class is your guide to turning raw bisque ware into vibrant, functional pieces you’ll be proud to use every day. We’ll demystify why we glaze in the first place—how it seals the clay, makes it food-safe, and brings color, depth, and durability to your work. From there, you’ll explore the many ways to apply glaze, including brushing, dipping, and layering techniques that create everything from smooth, even finishes to rich, dynamic surfaces. You’ll learn how to work with both glazes and underglazes, understanding when to use each and how they interact. We’ll cover essential best practices like keeping the bottoms clean (no one wants a kiln shelf disaster), how to properly handle and pay for glaze usage, and the importance of studio cleanup and care so everyone can create in a safe, shared space. This class is perfect for beginners or anyone ready to gain confidence in glazing. You’ll leave with the knowledge to make smart, creative choices—and beautifully finished pieces that are ready for the kiln and the table. Class syllabus • What is ceramic glaze • What are different type and style of glazes • What is underglaze and decal and how to utilize it in your works • Why we glaze and the meaning of food safe glazes • Reading labels and understanding cones • Why we bisque • Benefits of sanding our work • Why we clean our bisque before glazing • What are the different ways we can apply glaze • How to properly apply glazes with brushes • Importance of drying between coats • What are different type of brushes • How to layer glazes and avoid running • The importance of an unglazed foot and how to avoid sticking • Issue we will encounter such as crazing, crawling, pitting, blisters, etc • Ways to decorate after glaze is fired • Key points when using the MakerSpace glazes and Paying for you Glazes • Cleaning up and proper etiquette • How to makes cookies for your work • The importance of labeling

title: The Art & Science of Soap Making: Cold Process for Beginners $40
description: When Fri Oct 16 5:30pm — 7pm Central Where Lab - Science - Chemistry Details Handmade & One-of-a-Kind: Cold Process Soap Workshop Host Liam Luu Cost $0.00 Unlock the art and science of soap making in this can’t-miss, hands-on cold process workshop! In this engaging and beginner-friendly class, you’ll learn how to create beautiful, long-lasting bar soap from scratch using the cold process method—the gold standard for artisan soap makers. We’ll guide you step-by-step through the entire process, from selecting oils to safely working with lye, so you feel confident every step of the way. But this isn’t just about following a recipe—we’ll dive into the fascinating science of saponification, giving you a clear understanding of how simple ingredients transform into a gentle, effective cleansing bar. Once you understand the “why,” you’ll be empowered to experiment and create your own custom recipes. Then comes the fun: personalization! You’ll blend your own fragrance, choose your style, and craft a truly one-of-a-kind soap that reflects your creativity. By the end of the workshop, you won’t just leave with your own handmade soap curing and ready to use—you’ll walk away with the confidence, knowledge, and skills to become self-sufficient, making and customizing soap at home for yourself, your family, or even as gifts. Syllabus: -What is saponification -What are surfactant -Type of fats and oils in soap-making -Quality of each fat and oil -Saturated vs. Unsaturated fats -Type of lye; NaOH vs KOH -Hot Process vs Cold Process Soap -Step by Step instruction on making Soap -Adding Fragrance -Understanding pH -Aging your soap

title: Hardware Hacking:  Learn to Power Glitch!
description: When Thu Oct 22 6:30pm — 9pm Central Where Classroom - Interactive Details Unlock the hidden world of physical security by disrupting hardware execution in real time. Host Ian Wilson Cost $75.00 Software security measures are only as reliable as the hardware executing them. When firmware logic assumes stable hardware operations, physical fault injection—specifically power (voltage) glitching—can break those assumptions with extreme precision.In Hardware Hacking: Learn to Power Glitch!, you will dive into the practical mechanics of physical fault injection. Using the open-source ChipWhisperer toolchain, students will learn how briefly dropping a microcontroller's power rail forces the CPU to skip instructions, corrupt loop counters, and bypass authentication routines. Through guided, step-by-step lab exercises, participants will: * Master the core principles and timing mechanics of voltage fault injection. * Configure glitch triggers, pulse widths, and offsets using Python scripts. * Target embedded ARM microcontrollers to bypass password checks and dumped restricted memory. * Analyze physical hardware layout considerations, such as decoupling capacitor removal. Study software and hardware defensive countermeasures to mitigate glitch attacks. Whether you are a penetration tester, embedded developer, or hardware security enthusiast, this course provides actionable skills to evaluate and secure embedded devices against physical attack vectors. The Student Fee of $75 will include a ChipWhisperer-Nano (Retail Price $60), a STM32 BluePill (Retail Price $10) and some breadboards for easy prototyping (Retail Price $5). Students will need to have some electronics engineering experience, bring a laptop capable of installing the ChipWhisperer Library (ideally Linux), and be comfortable with the python programming language.

Please check out https://www.meetup.com/libretechnica/ for more details and a general list of monthly topics. Events are scheduled each month on every 3rd Wednesday.
